statements.text: These tools raise a significant concern of the agro, whatever, the bias—I can never say that word—digital surveillance, and data collection, and security. Data collection should scare all of us.
statements.context: Congressional hearing on AI applications in financial services and housing, where Rep. Tlaib questions a witness about landlord-use AI tools.

statements.text: What happens when AI models now—again, using this technology—are trained on historic or contemporary data that reflects past or present discrimination? Does not this risk create models that perpetuate or reinforce discriminatory practices? [...] Because it is teaching it to go around, telling on themselves.
statements.context: Congresswoman Tlaib speaks at a Financial Services Committee hearing on AI in financial services, focusing on discriminatory data practices in auto insurance.

statements.text: I am introducing a new bill, the No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act. Our bill would permanently ban large data centers on Federal lands, including military bases. It would also remove any existing qualifying AI data center and mandate site remediation to protect our health and our environment. [...] We should protect our public lands from data center destruction. [...] AI data centers bring noise, light, air, and water pollution. [...] We can tell this President that AI shouldn't be making military decisions and AI shouldn't trump our public health and our environmental laws.
statements.context: Verbatim floor speech in the House of Representatives introducing a bill to ban AI data centers on federal lands.
